title: The Helical SYK Model and Emergent Infrared Integrability
authors: Gustavo Valdivia-Mera, Bhavay Tyagi, Eric R. Bittner, Pavan Hosur
abstract: We construct a helical generalization of the Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model in $1+1$ dimensions, built from left- and right-moving Majorana fermions with local quartic interactions and random couplings in flavor-chirality space. These interactions organize into a symmetry-controlled hierarchy of quartic chirality sectors. At the most restrictive end of this hierarchy, symmetry forces the quartic structure into a density-density form, which admits an exact solution using bosonization, rendering the theory integrable. Once the full quartic helical interaction space is allowed, including purely chiral, chirality-balanced, and chirality-imbalanced sectors, this symmetry-protected integrable structure is lost. Nevertheless, the large-$N$ infrared limit remains analytically tractable through short-distance selection rules and disorder averaging. Using conformal perturbation theory about the free fixed point, we show that the entire interaction space is marginally irrelevant, and the theory thus becomes free and integrable in the IR.
summary: This paper analyzes a helical generalization of the SYK model, exploring how its random quartic interactions behave under renormalization group flow. While generic couplings destroy initial integrability, the disorder-averaged large-$N$ limit forces the system back to an exactly solvable, free, and integrable state in the infrared regime.
main_problem: The research investigates the emergence of infrared (IR) integrability in a generalized, random-coupled quantum chaotic model.
main_result: In the disorder-averaged large-$N$ IR limit, the theory re-emerges as integrable because all quartic interactions flow to zero due to conformal perturbation theory analysis. The system is exactly solvable when restricted by symmetries or in this deep IR limit.
method: The study employs bosonization, Conformal Perturbation Theory (CPT), and Renormalization Group (RG) flow analysis on a generalized Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK) model.
model_or_system: The system is a $1+1$ dimensional helical generalization of the SYK model built from left- and right-moving Majorana fermions with random quartic couplings in flavor-chirality space. The Hamiltonian structure is analyzed across various symmetry constraints, ranging from maximally symmetric to fully general.
key_observables: The primary observables are the RG flow coefficients (beta functions) determining coupling strength evolution, and the resulting physical energy density ($\epsilon_{	ext{phys}}$) in solvable limits.
important_parameters: Key parameters include the system size $N$, the disorder strengths $J_S$, and the dimensionality ($1+1$ dimensions). The analysis focuses on the large-$N$ limit.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes Gaussian random couplings for disorder averaging, relies on separating symmetry-constrained sectors from the full interaction space, and uses CPT around a free fixed point.
figures_summary: Figures likely summarize the hierarchy of symmetries constraining interactions (Table 2) and illustrate the flow equations or diagonalization results for normal modes.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the highly symmetric, exactly integrable sector via bosonization. It then analyzes how relaxing symmetries expands the interaction space. The core is the RG analysis showing that disorder averaging forces the system back to an IR fixed point where integrability is recovered through marginal irrelevance.
why_interesting: The connection between random interactions (disorder) and emergent exact solvability in the deep infrared limit is a powerful concept relevant to understanding thermalization and quantum chaos in many-body systems, which has parallels in AMO physics when studying complex interacting regimes.
